extracted.intended_audience: aspiring SNL hosts, comedy writers, production crew, and curious fans
extracted.subtask_description: A day-by-day timeline and practical guide describing the host's responsibilities, schedule, and interactions with writers, cast, and production across the week leading up to a live SNL episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall commitment and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting Saturday Night Live is hard; it's physically and emotionally demanding and requires giving up a week of your life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many potential hosts turn down the chance because the show is live and demanding. Every host who agrees to do it must work hard—it's a requirement of the job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monday: pitch meeting and initial introductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Host meets Lorne Michaels and the talent department and attends the 'pitch meeting' where cast and writers pitch sketch ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches are often ice-breakers to gauge what the host thinks is funny and aren't necessarily real sketches; occasionally a 'fake pitch' can evolve into a real sketch. Monday is generally a light, low-pressure day of a few hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuesday: fittings, face scan, digital promo
rubrics_metrics.description: Host gets fitted for wigs, undergoes a face scan, and shoots the digital promo—this takes about four hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers are penning sketches that night. The host can choose their level of involvement in brainstorming/writing. The host dinner (typically Tuesday night) is both mandatory and useful for relationship-building and guidance from Lorne.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host involvement in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A host can be as involved in the sketch-writing process as they wish, from active brainstorming with writers to no involvement at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the process isn't in the host's wheelhouse, they don't have to participate; but being involved can help tailor material to the host's strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host dinner as mandatory relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: The host dinner typically includes Lorne, the host, and a few writers and cast members and is both mandatory and fun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dinner helps everyone get to know the host better and for Lorne to help the host navigate the rest of the week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wednesday read-through procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-through day: host arrives ~1 p.m. to read ~40 sketches at a table while writers give notes in the host's dressing room beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read-through usually takes 3–4 hours. Afterward, producers, director, and head writers meet to select the ~11 sketches to produce. The atmosphere is low-pressure despite the volume of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cue card readability and sizing protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Cue cards come in two print sizes; the appropriate size is chosen based on the host's eyesight to balance readability and the number of words per card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sight is good, use regular-sized printing to allow more words and better rhythm; if eyesight is poor, use larger printing. The cue-card person (Wally) meets the host early to assess needs and avoid overwhelming them with information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cue card placement and 'playing' rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sets of cue cards are placed on a set (center, left, right); the host should 'play' the set closest to the cast member they're speaking to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also recommended to play the center set occasionally because most cameras are out in front, preventing the host from being shot mostly in profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thursday: ease-in rehearsal strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Thursday rehearsals focus on blocking and rehearsing four of the 'easier' sketches (minimal blocking for host) to ease the host into the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This day also includes episode bumper photos and network promos. Thursday is a roughly 10-hour day but intended to be a relatively relaxed introduction to onstage rehearsal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friday: intense production day (digital shoots, choreography, monologue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Friday is busy: early start (around 6 a.m.) for digital video shoots (often finishing mid-afternoon), followed by blocking/rehearsing remaining sketches, dance rehearsals with choreographer, wardrobe fittings, voiceovers, and monologue work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically two sketches are finished before dinner; after dinner they finish the rest with the monologue usually last. Hosts review line changes with writers and Steve Higgins late into the night.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturday: run-throughs, dress rehearsal, and live show
rubrics_metrics.description: Saturday begins ~12:30 p.m. with run-throughs in as much wardrobe/wigs as possible, a dinner break during the musical act's sound check, rehearsal of cold open and Weekend Update, dress rehearsal 8–10 p.m., and the live show at 11:30 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After dress, Lorne, producers, and the host decide which sketches make the live show; the live show often flies by. Hosts usually have some time during Saturday because they rarely appear in cold open or Weekend Update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: producers pick sketches to produce
rubrics_metrics.description: After Wednesday read-through, producers, director, and head writers pick the 11 sketches for production from the ~40-read list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions about which sketches will be in the live show and which will be cut are made after dress rehearsal, with Lorne leading a meeting to go over changes and fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error preparedness and team corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes happen across rehearsals and the live show, and Lorne leads reviews addressing mistakes by actors, director, lighting, sound, and cue cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone aims to minimize errors during the live show; post-decision meetings are used to address and fix production mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-show celebration norm
rubrics_metrics.description: After the live broadcast, cast and crew attend a cast party where the host is celebrated for surviving the week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party is a way to wind down, celebrate the week's work, and for the host to reconnect and be applauded by the cast and crew; many hosts are eager to be asked back.
